backlog.spec: In cons inside _solve_once, scale the pairwise constraint by dividing d by (r_i + r_j + 0.05). This keeps its sign and makes its magnitude comparable across pairs. Multiply the wall and radius-nonnegativity constraints by 10 so that they are of similar scale to the pair terms. Scaling an inequality by a positive factor does not change the feasible set, but it changes how SLSQP weights the constraints and can help it converge to better local optima. Repair stays the same. Change nothing else.
backlog.title: Constraint scaling for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Two changes. (1) In _solve_once, when start is None, with probability 0.5 pick the initial centres by farthest-point sampling from 400 uniform candidates in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2 (first random, then repeatedly the candidate with the largest minimum distance to the chosen set). (2) Pass exact derivatives to SLSQP: jac of the objective is zeros for the 2n centre entries and -1 for the n radius entries; the constraint Jacobian is a dense (m, 3n) array built with vectorised index assignment: for pair k = (i, j), the derivative with respect to c_i is (c_i - c_j)/dist, with respect to c_j the negative, and -1 for r_i and r_j (guard dist with max(dist, 1e-12)); the wall rows are +1 or -1 on the centre coordinate and -1 on the radius; the last n rows are +1 on the radius. Analytic gradients alone were neutral in the pure-restart script (slot 3); here the test is whether the extra speed gives more perturbation trials on top of better starts.
backlog.title: Maximin starts with analytic Jacobian for more trials

backlog.spec: Lower SHRINK from 1e-9 to 2e-11. After repair, verify exactly in double precision: all pair distances >= r_i+r_j and walls hold with c-r>=0 and c+r<=1. If any check fails, subtract 1e-10 from all radii and retest, up to 5 times. The harness tolerance is 1e-10, so the gain is small but free.
backlog.title: Smaller SHRINK with verified repair

backlog.spec: Add maximin starts for half of the fresh starts: when start is None and rng.random()<0.5, draw 400 candidates uniform in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2, pick a random first candidate, then repeatedly add the candidate that maximizes the minimum distance to the chosen points until there are n centres. Radii stay at INIT_RADIUS. Also, in solve, change the switch to the perturbation phase from 0.3*TIME_FRACTION*time_limit to 0.15*TIME_FRACTION*time_limit. Nothing else changes.
backlog.title: Maximin starts with restart share 15%

backlog.spec: Keep the top 4 distinct packings found by restarts. For a fraction of the perturbation steps, choose two elites at random. Draw a random line through the unit square, take the circles of the first parent on one side and the circles of the second parent on the other side, and fix the total count at n by dropping or adding the smallest-radius circles, with new circles placed at random. Run the existing SLSQP polish with a short iteration cap on the child, then repair. Accept the child into the elite set if it beats the worst elite and is not a duplicate.
backlog.title: Cut-and-splice crossover of elite packings

backlog.spec: For fresh random starts in _solve_once, draw the centre coordinates from a Latin hypercube over [INIT_LOW, 1 - INIT_LOW] instead of i.i.d. uniform. Use n strata per axis, shuffle each axis independently with rng.permutation, and place one sample in each stratum with a uniform offset inside it. Keep the radius initialisation and the warm-start branch unchanged, so the only change is how the starting centres are spread.
backlog.title: Latin-hypercube starting centres

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, with probability 1/3, use a window move instead of the current moves. Pick a random point p uniform in [0.15,0.85]^2. Take the k=5 to 7 circles whose centres are nearest to p, put them at new positions p + rng.uniform(-0.15,0.15,(k,2)) clipped to [0.02,0.98], and set their radii to 0.02. Keep all other circles as they are in the best packing. Then run the full SLSQP from this x0 with MAX_ITER. The other two thirds keep the current 50/50 relocate-2-3/jitter moves. Accept only if better, as now.
backlog.title: Large-neighbourhood re-solve of a spatial window

backlog.spec: Half of fresh starts use staggered rows: choose a row count k from {5,6} and per-row counts that sum to 26 with entries 4-6, placed evenly in y and x with a half-spacing offset on alternate rows, plus gaussian jitter sd 0.03, initial radius 0.06. The other half use maximin starts. Perturbation phase unchanged.
backlog.title: Hex-row starts with random row counts

backlog.spec: Add the slot-34 maximin start: in _solve_once with start None and rng.random()<0.5, take 400 candidates from rng.uniform(INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW, (400,2)), choose a random first one, then greedily add the candidate with the largest minimum distance to the chosen set until there are n. In the perturbation branch (start not None), add a third move with probability 1/3: c0 = clip(c0 + rng.normal(0, 0.05, c0.shape), 0.01, 0.99), keep r0, and run SLSQP with maxiter 60 instead of MAX_ITER (pass maxiter as an argument to _solve_once). The other two thirds keep the current 50/50 relocate/jitter moves at full MAX_ITER. Repair and the accept-if-better logic stay the same.
backlog.title: Maximin starts plus shake-all perturbation

backlog.spec: Give each random restart its own SLSQP iteration cap, drawn log-uniformly from [40, 400] using rng. Short caps let many starts be screened cheaply, and long caps let good starts converge. Keep the existing best-so-far update rule. Do not change the perturbation phase, which keeps MAX_ITER.
backlog.title: Random per-restart iteration budget

backlog.spec: Change only how fresh random starts (start is None in _solve_once) pick centres; draw the start type uniformly from three options. (a) Uniform as now. (b) Maximin: draw 400 uniform candidates in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2 and pick n by farthest-point sampling (first point random, then repeatedly the candidate with the largest minimum distance to the chosen set). (c) Ring plus maximin interior: place 12 circles on the perimeter, 3 per wall at evenly spaced positions along the wall with jitter of sd 0.03, at distance uniform(0.03, 0.12) from that wall, then pick the other 14 centres by farthest-point sampling from 400 candidates in [0.2, 0.8]^2, where the distance is measured to all chosen points including the ring. Initial radii stay INIT_RADIUS. Leave the perturbation phase and repair unchanged.
backlog.title: Maximin starts mixed with perimeter-ring starts

backlog.spec: Run SLSQP in two stages for each fresh start: 40 iterations first, then 160 more from the result, with centres from maximin sampling (best of 400 candidates). Slots 15 and 34 each looked helpful on their own. Perturbation phase unchanged.
backlog.title: Two-stage SLSQP with maximin starts

backlog.spec: Multiply pair-distance constraints by 1.0 and the wall and radius-positivity constraints by 1.0, but divide the objective by n (use -mean radius times 10) so SLSQP's line search is better conditioned. Equivalently scale the objective to -sum(r)/n*10. Nothing else changes. Check that the repair step still gives valid packings.
backlog.title: Scale constraints for SLSQP

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, keep the current packing as the chain state instead of always returning to the global best. After each perturbation and SLSQP polish with repair, accept the candidate if its radius sum is higher, or with probability exp((new_sum - cur_sum) / T) otherwise. Set T to 0.003 at the start of the phase and decay it geometrically to 1e-5 by the time limit. Always record the global best separately and return it. Use rng for all draws.
backlog.title: Metropolis acceptance in the perturbation chain

backlog.spec: For half of fresh starts use maximin centres, and for the other half place 12 circles in a jittered perimeter ring (distance 0.03-0.08 from the walls, evenly spaced along the boundary with jitter) and the remaining 14 at random in [0.2,0.8]^2. Initial radii 0.05. Keep the rest unchanged.
backlog.title: Maximin starts with perimeter ring

backlog.spec: Keep the search as it is. Stop the loop at 0.75*time_limit instead of TIME_FRACTION. Then take the best packing (its unrepaired centres and radii) and run one SLSQP from it with options {'maxiter': 1000, 'ftol': 1e-13}. Repair the result with _repair and return it only if its sum beats the stored best. Also store the unrepaired SLSQP output next to the best repaired packing, so that the polish starts from the raw optimum and not from the shrunk radii. Guard the polish so that it starts only if at least 4 s of CPU time remain.
backlog.title: Final SLSQP polish with tight tolerance before repair

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, maintain a noise scale sigma starting at 0.02 for the Gaussian shake of the chosen circles. Count successes (candidate beats the current chain state). Every 10 perturbations, multiply sigma by 1.2 if the success rate over that window exceeded 0.2, otherwise multiply by 0.83, and clip sigma to [0.003, 0.08]. Keep the existing move types and the existing SLSQP polish; only the step size becomes adaptive.
backlog.title: 1/5-rule adaptive perturbation step size

backlog.spec: Two changes. (1) In _solve_once, when start is None, with probability 0.5 pick the initial centres by farthest-point sampling from 400 uniform candidates in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2 (first point random, then repeatedly the candidate with the largest minimum distance to those already chosen) instead of uniform draws. (2) In solve, replace the hard-coded 0.3 with a new constant RESTART_SHARE = 0.2, so perturbation of the best packing starts after 20% of the usable time instead of 30%. The idea is that better starts need fewer restarts to find a good basin, leaving more time to refine it.
backlog.title: Maximin starts with a 20% restart share

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, for a third of moves choose a random point in the square, take the 6 circles nearest to it, re-randomise their centres uniformly within a disc of radius 0.2 around the point, set their radii to 0.03, and run SLSQP on all circles with maxiter 100. Accept if the repaired sum improves. Other moves stay the same.
backlog.title: Large-neighbourhood window re-solve

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed 30 percent switch point with a stall rule. Keep running random restarts, and track how many consecutive restarts fail to improve the best radius sum. Once that count reaches 8, or 60 percent of the budget has been used, switch to the perturbation search from the best packing. The minimum restart phase is 10 percent of the budget. Everything else stays the same.
backlog.title: Stall-triggered switch from restarts to perturbation
